Customer: provide representative traffic CSV and typical prompt sets by 2027-06-24
Schedule 1h benchmark kickoff run with GPU pool (reserved + burst) 2027-06-28
action_items: Diego Ramos: prepare k6 load profile and tokenization script; run small smoke test by 2027-06-22
Priya Natarajan: share SSO/SAML and KMS contact for compliance review by 2027-06-24

header:
Date: 2027-06-21
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~72 minutes
Attendees: Amelia Park (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Nadia Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Natarajan (Mistral), Liam O'Connor (Mistral), Sofie Berg (Mistral), Rajesh Patel (Mistral)
summary: Kickoff for a 4-week POC to validate capacity sizing and autoscale/fallback behavior. Primary goals: confirm reserved GPU sizing for baseline throughput, define burst capacity strategy and acceptable fallback models, validate latency SLOs (p50/p95/p99), and agree on benchmark plan and timeline.
transcript:
[00:00] Amelia Park: okay hi everyone uh thanks for joining, this is Amelia from Redwood, um quick round of intros?
[00:08] Priya Natarajan: Priya here, head of platform at Mistral Consortium. We own the inference infra for the consortium projects.
[00:13] Liam O'Connor: Liam - ML Infra. We run a mix of synchronous chat APIs and async batch embedding jobs.
[00:18] Diego Ramos: Diego, Redwood SE - I'll be running the benchmarks with you.
[00:22] Sofie Berg: Sofie - security. I'll be skimming compliance bits.
[00:25] Rajesh Patel: Rajesh - product, coordinating success criteria.
[00:28] Amelia Park: Great. High level: we want to scope a POC that proves we can meet your latency SLOs during normal traffic on a reserved pool, and fail over gracefully to burst capacity or a smaller, cheaper model if reserved is exhausted. Are those the right outcomes?
[00:44] Priya Natarajan: yes, exactly. Our must-haves: p95 generation latency below 400ms for 8k context chat on the production prompt set, and a cost target per 1k tokens. Also strict audit logs and KMS integration.
[01:02] Diego Ramos: okay, couple clarifying q's - when you say "8k context chat" is that average session length or max?
[01:07] Liam O'Connor: typical session is 2.5k tokens, bursts to 8k for long docs. We do about 120 concurrent chat sessions at peak for product A, plus intermittent heavy embedding spikes up to 2k concurrent jobs.
[01:20] Amelia Park: good, that'll drive our reserved sizing. For the POC we usually emulate your peak for a 2-hour run and then a stress window where we push 2x peak for 30 minutes to observe tail behavior.
[01:34] Priya Natarajan: timeline question: can we finish benchmarks within two weeks? We have a steering review on 2027-07-08.
[01:40] Diego Ramos: timeline is tight but doable. Week 0 - config and wiring (SSO/KMS/ent logs), Week 1 - baseline reserved runs, Week 2 - burst/fallback tests and analysis.
[01:51] Sofie Berg: on compliance, we need SOC2 type II report, encryption at rest with our KMS, and audit log retention for 1 year. Is that in your standard private package?
[02:02] Amelia Park: yes, Redwood Private supports customer KMS/HSM and audit logs. We'll send the compliance pack; Diego can add the specific endpoints that show audit log delivery.
[02:11] Rajesh Patel: Can you talk about the actual capacity mix? like how many GPUs for reserved vs burst pools?
[02:16] Diego Ramos: Sure. Based on initial numbers—if you pinned a 8k context 1.3B-ish model variant, throughput per A100-ish GPU is roughly 30-40 tokens/sec stable with our optimized runtime. For your 120 concurrent sessions at 2.5k tokens avg, that's ~300k tokens in-flight. For p95 latency under 400ms we'd recommend reserving a pool equivalent to 6 GPUs for the baseline, and configuring burst that can add up to +4 GPUs from a shared burst pool. But that's a rough starting point, we need to run your prompt set as throughput and cache behavior change that.
[02:53] Liam O'Connor: hold on, 30-40 tokens/sec seems low to our internal numbers, we get like 60-80 tokens/sec per GPU for similar models when we run custom kernels. Could be due to different batching or KV cache patterns.
[03:05] Diego Ramos: yeah totally, kernel selection and quantization matter. Our numbers assume some safety margin and real-world multi-tenant overhead. We'll run the same model artifacts you use to get exact parity.
[03:15] Nadia Chen: also important: prefix caching across sessions can cut token generation by ~20% depending on prompt overlap; we need your conversation templates to model that.
[03:24] Priya Natarajan: we'll share a sampled prompt set with masked PII.
[03:28] Amelia Park: perfect. Now fallback strategies - typical patterns are: 1) queueing with backpressure and user-visible "temporarily degraded" mode, 2) auto-failing to a smaller quantized model variant, 3) regional failover to another data center. Which do you prefer?
[03:43] Rajesh Patel: product prefers reduced-quality fallback (small model) over queuing - user experience team worried about long queues.
[03:51] Sofie Berg: security also flags cross-region failover because of data residency - we need to limit cross-region fallback for certain customer datasets.
[03:58] Amelia Park: noted. So for POC we'll demonstrate 2 and 3 but with data residency gating: fallback to smaller model in same region is default, cross-region only for non-sensitive datasets. We'll show policy-based routing.
[04:14] Diego Ramos: operationally we'll implement an in-line policy: if reserved pool saturates and burst capacity is available, route to burst; if burst saturated, route to quantized-variant; if still saturated, return 429 with graceful message. We'll instrument per-route counters and a canary that sends 5% of traffic to fallback during rolling deploys.
[04:33] Liam O'Connor: what's the expected latency delta for the quantized variant?
[04:37] Diego Ramos: depends on quantization and model size - roughly 1.5-2x slower p95 for very small models but overall token cost is lower. We'll put numbers in the benchmark report.
[04:48] Priya Natarajan: can Redwood run the tests to simulate your 2x-peak stress with realistic token distributions? We can provide the CSV.
[04:55] Diego Ramos: yes, we'll use k6 or Locust with tokenization-aware clients. We'll run three scenarios: baseline (normal traffic), ramp-to-peak, and stress (2x for 30m). We'll capture p50/p95/p99 latencies, GPU utilization, queue lengths, and cost delta.
[05:11] Amelia Park: on observability, you'll get per-route dashboards, token-level cost, and trace links. We'll also export a raw CSV of token events if you want to ingest into your own observability.
[05:20] Sofie Berg: need to validate audit log format and retention during POC - can we get a sample delivery endpoint?
[05:25] Diego Ramos: yes we'll provide an S3 HTTPS webhook example and a small script to validate event contents.
[05:32] Priya Natarajan: about pricing: reserved monthly commitment vs on-demand burst - can you show the delta on a per-1M token basis?
[05:39] Amelia Park: we'll prepare a pricing matrix. For the POC, we'll use a short-lived reserved allocation (30 days) so you can see unit economics. We'll send both a 6-month reserved estimate and the POC term.
[05:50] Rajesh Patel: ok acceptance criteria - I want a clear pass/fail: 1) p95 <= 400ms for 8k context under baseline peak; 2) during 2x stress p99 should not exceed 2s for >95% of requests (we can tolerate a small tail); 3) fallback must return either a quantized variant response or a 429 with correct audit log entry; 4) KMS integration verified.
[06:12] Amelia Park: solid. We'll translate those into test assertions in the benchmark harness.
[06:17] Diego Ramos: one more operational detail - autoscale policy: we'll demonstrate a target-based autoscaler keyed on queue length and GPU utilization with a cooldown of 60s, scaling up in steps of 1 GPU and scale-down after 300s. We'll show alternatives if you want more aggressive scaling.
[06:32] Liam O'Connor: cooldowns are fine but we need predictable billing. Can we limit burst to a daily cap to avoid runaway costs?
[06:38] Amelia Park: yes, burst caps and per-hour spend limits are standard; we'll set a conservative cap for POC.
[06:44] Sofie Berg: any known gotchas around KV cache and multi-tenant interference?
[06:49] Diego Ramos: KV cache eviction patterns can cause latency spikes when many sessions share ephemeral contexts; for POC we'll instrument cache hit ratios and recommend cache sizing or session affinity.
[06:58] Priya Natarajan: good to know. For the benchmark, please include a run with and without cache warming.
[07:03] Diego Ramos: will do.
[07:05] Amelia Park: ok let's recap next steps, who owns what.
[07:09] Diego Ramos: Redwood will: 1) share benchmark harness repo and default k6 scenario by 2027-06-22, 2) provision a reserved GPU pool for POC (6 GPUs) and temporary burst limit (+4 GPUs) for the runs on 2027-06-28, 3) run baseline and stress tests and deliver a results pack by 2027-07-02.
[07:28] Priya Natarajan: Mistral Consortium will: 1) provide masked prompt set and traffic CSV by 2027-06-24, 2) confirm which datasets are region-restricted by 2027-06-25, 3) provide SSO/KMS contacts for access by 2027-06-24.
[07:44] Rajesh Patel: and we'll want a follow-up review meeting 2027-07-05 to go over results ahead of steering review.
[07:51] Amelia Park: scheduled; I'll send a calendar invite. Any other questions?
[07:55] Sofie Berg: one tiny thing - can we see an example of the fallback message to users? Product needs copy.
[08:00] Amelia Park: yup we'll include example UX copy in the results pack.
[08:03] Liam O'Connor: great, thanks everyone.
[08:05] Priya Natarajan: thanks.
[08:07] Amelia Park: thanks all, bye.

Notes: occasional transcription errors in model names and kernel specifics; references to benchmark artifacts: https://redwood.example.com/poc/mistral/bench-harness (placeholder), and a shared spreadsheet for cost modeling (link to be emailed).

End of transcript.
